title: Night Light System Tray toggle does not function after Night Light has been turned off with a keyboard shortcut
line: After suspending Night Light with its keyboard shortcut, the Brightness and Color widget's switch can resume it again.
explanation: KWin's Suspend/Resume Night Light shortcut used a global inhibition, the same mechanism apps use with a cookie. The brightness applet can't lift an inhibition it doesn't own, so it greyed out its switch and showed 'Suspended' until the shortcut was pressed again. The shortcut now suspends Night Light through the manual deactivation state added for the applet ('Suspended until manually resumed') and resumes by clearing any temporary (de)activation, still showing the Suspended/Resumed OSD. The applet then shows the switch as on and clicking it (or middle-clicking the icon) resumes Night Light.

commits.message:
plugins/nightlight: suspend with the shortcut until manually resumed

The Suspend/Resume shortcut inhibited Night Light globally, which the
brightness applet can't lift, so its switch was greyed out until the
shortcut was used again. The shortcut now uses manual deactivation.

BUG: 487617

media.caption: After the shortcut: Night Light 'Suspended', switch greyed out (master, tester's run)
Clicking the switch does nothing; it stays suspended
After the shortcut: 'Suspended until manually resumed', switch enabled and on
Clicking the switch resumes Night Light (On, 4,500K)

review.text: It addresses the cause: the shortcut now uses the same manual deactivation state that the applet can undo, instead of a global inhibition only KWin owns. It reuses tryActivateOrDeactivate and keeps the OSD. One behaviour change to mention in the MR: the shortcut's suspension now persists across a KWin restart, which matches the applet's 'until manually resumed'. The media show the switch enabled and working.
